item.research_question: Can the radiative thermal load of colored objects be controlled and tuned for thermal management purposes?
item.material_system: Photonic structures made of one-dimensional thin film stacks, including silicon (Si), silicon dioxide (SiO2), titanium dioxide (TiO2), and chromium (Cr)
item.processing_route: Electron beam deposition, with optimization of layer thicknesses using a memetic algorithm
item.test_conditions: Outdoor environment, with solar irradiance and ambient air temperature measured using a pyranometer and a resistance temperature detector probe
key_findings: The radiative thermal load of colored objects can be tuned over a range of at least 680 Wm−2
Objects with the same color can have drastically different thermal loads due to effects of metamerism, infrared solar absorption, and radiative cooling
The temperature difference between two photonic structures with the same pink color can be as high as 47.6 °C under sunlight
The hotter photonic structure can be 10 °C hotter than a commercial black paint
The colder photonic structure can be 22.6 °C colder than a commercial pink paint
item.mechanism: The authors explain that the tunable range of radiative thermal load is due to the physical effects of infrared solar absorption and radiative cooling, as well as the physiological effect of metamerism
quotes: the colours of outdoor structures, such as automobiles, buildings and clothing, are typically chosen for functional or aesthetic reasons
the range exceeds 680 Wm−2 for all colours, and can be as high as 866 Wm−2

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can the radiative thermal load of colored objects be controlled and tuned for thermal management purposes?. System: Photonic structures made of one-dimensional thin film stacks, including silicon (Si), silicon dioxide (SiO2), titanium dioxide (TiO2), and chromium (Cr). Processing: Electron beam deposition, with optimization of layer thicknesses using a memetic algorithm. Test conditions: Outdoor environment, with solar irradiance and ambient air temperature measured using a pyranometer and a resistance temperature detector probe. Findings: The radiative thermal load of colored objects can be tuned over a range of at least 680 Wm−2; Objects with the same color can have drastically different thermal loads due to effects of metamerism, infrared solar absorption, and radiative cooling; The temperature difference between two photonic structures with the same pink color can be as high as 47.6 °C under sunlight; The hotter photonic structure can be 10 °C hotter than a commercial black paint; The colder photonic structure can be 22.6 °C colder than a commercial pink paint. Mechanism: The authors explain that the tunable range of radiative thermal load is due to the physical effects of infrared solar absorption and radiative cooling, as well as the physiological effect of metamerism. Quote: "the colours of outdoor structures, such as automobiles, buildings and clothing, are typically chosen for functional or aesthetic reasons"
